summary: Dashboard panel edit fails when linked trace hook includes custom trace header
description: Issue summary: Customer reported 500 error when attempting to edit a dashboard panel that has a linked trace hook. Impact: Customer cannot update thresholds or annotations on affected panels; blocks release of dashboard changes for 12 teams at QuantaHealth. Observed behavior: Edit modal fails to load and the console returns a 500 response when the panel's linked trace hook contains a custom header 'X-Trace-Token' with length > 128 bytes. Expected behavior: Panel edit should open normally regardless of trace hook headers; tracing links should continue to surface without causing edit failures.
impact: Multiple dashboards uneditable for key customer org; potential rollback of dashboard changes; frustrated customer CS escalation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Log into console as an org admin for a customer in prod: us-east.
2) Navigate to Dashboards > select a panel that has a linked trace hook (Trace Hook configured under panel settings).
3) Ensure the linked trace hook is configured to inject a custom header 'X-Trace-Token' with a payload of ~200 bytes.
5) Observe the edit modal failing to load and a 500 error in the console network tab (XHR to /api/panels/:id/edit returns 500).
6) Temporarily remove or truncate the header value and retry; edit succeeds.
7) Recreate header content length to confirm threshold behavior (fails when >128 bytes, succeeds when <=128 bytes).
logs: [2026-03-11T14:02:03Z] console-frontend ERROR GET /api/panels/ids/edit 500 0.012s - TraceID=trc_9f3e - payload_error: header_overflow
[2026-03-11T14:02:03Z] gateway-1 WARN request_id=req-7c1a - downstream returned 500 (error parsing hook headers)
stack: Error: header value too long at parseTraceHookHeaders (hooks/middleware.js:132:27)
comments: 2026-03-11 | Samantha Lee: Customer QuantaHealth reported they could not edit 8 dashboards this morning; provided sample trace hook configuration with 'X-Trace-Token' value (200 bytes). Attached screenshot of 500 modal.

2026-03-11 | Support Triage (Miguel Torres): Reproduced in prod:us-east with supplied hook. Filed this bug and linked INT-1198 for infra investigation of header parsing middleware. Marking P1 due to customer impact.
2026-03-12 | SRE (Nina Gupta): Observed gateway returning 413-like internal error when header length >128. Hypothesis: header buffer capped in API gateway plugin introduced in 2026-03-05 deploy.

2026-03-12 | Dev (Luis Fernandez): Confirmed failing unit in hooks/middleware that assumes header length < 128. Working on a patch to validate and safely truncate headers before parsing. PR opened github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/8421.
2026-03-12 | Support: Notified QuantaHealth that we have a patch in review and provided a temporary workaround to truncate the header value in their trace hook configuration.
2026-03-12 | QuantaHealth (Customer): We applied the header truncation workaround and can edit panels again. Please advise ETA for permanent fix and whether this affects other customers.
investigation_notes: Reproduction validated in prod:us-east using customer payload. Failure point is parseTraceHookHeaders in console backend middleware.
Change window correlates with API gateway plugin update on 2026-03-05 that added stricter header buffer allocation (see INT-1198).
Headers with length >128 bytes cause Buffer.alloc to throw in Node layer; middleware did not catch exception, resulting in 500 surfaced to UI.
Scope: Likely impacts any org using custom trace-hook headers with long tokens or encoded payloads. Quick scan shows ~7 customers with similar hook configs across us-east.
Risk: No data corruption; symptom is UI 500 only when editing panels that enumerate the linked trace hook metadata.
Mitigation: truncating header or switching to server-side lookup avoids the code path that parses long header values.
Related items: INT-1198 (gateway header cap regression), SUP-712345 (customer reported similar but for trace link rendering; may be sibling symptom).
resolution: Workaround: Customer truncated 'X-Trace-Token' to <=128 bytes in their trace hook payload and regained edit capability. Temporary mitigation scripts provided for org admins. Fix: Patch merged and deployed to staging; consolidated patch validates header length and gracefully handles over-length headers by storing a stable truncated fingerprint; gateway plugin update reverted in us-east pending canary. Permanent fix in PR github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/8421; rollout scheduled to prod:us-east on 2026-03-14 with canary and monitoring.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12: Hotfix PR created to add defensive checks and avoid throwing on long headers.
2026-03-13: Reverted gateway plugin change in us-east to prevent new occurrences while fix is validated.
2026-03-14: Patch will be rolled to 10% canary, monitor for 2 hours; then full rollout if no regressions.

Follow-up: Add unit tests for header boundary cases; add a console telemetry alert for 'header_overflow' errors; notify customers with custom trace-hook headers and recommend max token length in docs.
Owner for follow-up: Miguel Torres (Support) and Luis Fernandez (Backend)
Postmortem task: INT ticket to track gateway plugin hardening (INT-1198).
